native_delegation.instruction: Use native delegation aggressively for parallelizable work that meets the criteria in the implement prompt. The parent session remains accountable for Striatum artifacts, write scope, verification, and completion.
Use sub-agents aggressively for bounded independent research, review, and code/test/doc authorship. Do not let native delegation obscure the parent session's artifact and verdict accountability.
Use local sub-agents only for bounded independent work. Do not rely on remote agent-to-agent delegation or hidden state as provenance.

jobs.title: Design RFC 0034 workflow generator from Codex
jobs.objective: Produce an implementation design for RFC 0034: workflow generator + template catalog. Focus on the public Python API (`generate_workflow(spec) -> GeneratedWorkflow`), shape compilers, lane-set compilers, custom-plan compiler with closed block vocabulary, local catalog package data, CLI surface (`workflow templates list/show`, `workflow generate`), local service read endpoints and mutation-gated generation endpoints (`POST /workflows/generate/preview` and `POST /workflows/generate`), and the relationship to existing `workflow init --style` and the RFC 0024 visual builder. The design must keep generation JSON-only and immediately valid under `workflow validate`. State which lane modifiers (`supervised`, `worktree_isolated`, `constrained`, `harness_profiled`) layer onto which lane sets without combinatorial explosion.

jobs.title: Design RFC 0034 workflow generator from Claude Code
jobs.objective: Produce an implementation design for RFC 0034 emphasizing the first-time-user experience: the choose-shape -> choose-lane-set -> fill-required-fields -> preview-graph -> review-JSON -> save flow. Cover the CLI ergonomics (clear required vs optional flags, helpful error messages with field_path, dry-run-by-default safety), the web `/workflows/new` chooser flow, and the local API surface that AI/operator-surrogate clients call so CLI/UI/chat tools all share one generator with one envelope. Discoverability matters: how does a first-time operator find templates, understand which shape fits, and not get stuck on combinatorial choice paralysis?

jobs.title: Design RFC 0034 workflow generator from Gemini
jobs.objective: Produce an implementation design for RFC 0034 with attention to: catalog metadata shape (shape entries and lane-set entries; `kind`, `display_name`, `summary`, `recommended_for`, `required_options`, `graph_preview`), the custom-plan compiler's closed block vocabulary and edge/cycle safety rules, lane-modifier compatibility matrix (which modifiers are valid against which lane sets, with field-specific errors for incompatible combinations), and the GeneratedWorkflow envelope shape returned identically by Python API + CLI + local API. Address generation-time validation: every generated workflow.json must immediately pass `workflow validate` or the generator returns a structured error. Cover the `--dry-run` semantics and the path-safety/overwrite-refusal posture for non-dry-run writes.

jobs.title: Synthesize RFC 0034 workflow generator implementation plan
jobs.objective: Reconcile all three fresh design artifacts into one implementation plan for RFC 0034. Choose the concrete WorkflowGenerationSpec schema, the catalog file layout (`src/striatum/workflow_templates/catalog.json` or package-data tree), the public Python API shape, the CLI surface, the local service API endpoints, and the custom-plan compiler's closed block vocabulary. EXPLICITLY DEFER the web chooser UI (`/workflows/new`) and the chat-assisted scaffolding tool to a follow-up dogfood; the dogfood-036 V1 slice ships the generator core, catalog, CLI surface, local API endpoints, and custom-plan compiler — UI and chat tool land later. State the deferred coverage clearly.

jobs.title: Ergonomics-DX review of RFC 0034 design
jobs.objective: Review the synthesized workflow-generator plan under the ergonomics_dx posture. Verdict acceptance means the affordances are discoverable and consistent from a first-time-user perspective. Evaluate: are the CLI verbs intuitive (`workflow templates list/show`, `workflow generate`)? Are required vs optional flags clear? Do error messages include `field_path` so the operator can fix a spec without scraping prose? Is `--dry-run` the safe default the operator reaches for first? Does the catalog metadata (`recommended_for`, `summary`, `display_name`) actually help a first-time operator pick a shape, or is it boilerplate? Is the Python API signature symmetric with the CLI and local API envelopes? Does `workflow init --style` still work as a familiar entry point for existing users? The web UI chooser and chat-assisted scaffolding tool are EXPLICITLY DEFERRED to a follow-up dogfood; do not refuse the design for their absence as long as the synthesis lists them as deferred coverage with clear pointers.

jobs.title: Implement RFC 0034 workflow generator V1 slice
jobs.objective: Implement only the reviewed and accepted V1 slice from docs/dogfood/036/DESIGN_SYNTHESIS.md. The web chooser UI and chat-assisted scaffolding tool are EXPLICITLY DEFERRED to a follow-up dogfood. Ship: generator core (`src/striatum/workflow_generator.py` or module of equivalent shape), built-in shapes + lane sets, package-data catalog, CLI surface (`workflow templates list/show`, `workflow generate`), local service read endpoints + mutation-gated generation endpoints, custom-plan compiler with closed block vocabulary, and immediate validation of every generated workflow.json. Rewire `workflow init --style` to dispatch through `generate_workflow` while preserving backwards-compatible output shape. Use sub-agents aggressively for parallelizable work per the implement prompt. Cycle exhaustion at max_iterations=2 -> operator records a decision artifact and continues with the latest verdict; do not block the run.

jobs.title: Ergonomics-DX review of RFC 0034 V1 build
jobs.objective: Review the implementation under the ergonomics_dx posture. Verdict acceptance means the affordances are discoverable and consistent from a first-time-operator perspective. Actually try the surfaces: run `striatum workflow templates list --json`, `striatum workflow templates show <id>`, `striatum workflow generate --dry-run --shape <s> --lane-set <l> ...`, and inspect the generated file tree. Verify: clear help text on every new CLI verb; required-flag errors name the missing field with `field_path`; `--dry-run` is the safe-default mode (writes nothing); non-dry-run writes refuse overwrite; the GeneratedWorkflow envelope is the same shape from Python API, CLI `--json`, and local API responses; immediate workflow validation runs before return; `workflow init --style` still works and dispatches through the generator. The web UI chooser and chat-assisted scaffolding tool are EXPLICITLY DEFERRED; do not refuse the build for their absence as long as the BUILD_HANDOFF documents the deferral with a pointer.
